Publisher/conference/journal: IEEE, Ninth International Conference on Social Networks Analysis, Management and Security (SNAMS), pp. 1–5
Dataset: UCI Drug Reviews with manually created summaries for reviews of 500 drugs; BBC News used as an additional benchmark
Method/model: Fine-tuned T5-small text-to-text transformer for abstractive summarization
Evaluation metrics: ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L; three-run averages and 95% confidence intervals
Major findings: Reported average ROUGE-1/2/L scores were 45.62/25.58/36.53 on drug reviews and 69.05/59.70/52.97 on BBC News, showing a large dependence on domain and reference-set size.
Limitations: Only 500 drug groups received labor-intensive human summaries; full IEEE access depends on institutional entitlement. Metadata and an author-uploaded copy were reviewed; users should verify the publisher-formatted IEEE copy through their institute.
Relevance to this project: Supports the optional CPU-oriented T5/BART-family abstractive branch and the use of ROUGE plus repeated evaluation.
Research gap identified: Needs larger, news-specific, diverse reference sets and explicit factual-consistency/latency evaluation.

Authors: N. Balaji; Deepa Kumari; N. Bhavatarini; N. Megha; P. Sunil Kumar; A. Shikah Rai
Publisher/conference/journal: IEEE, International Conference on Distributed Computing, VLSI, Electrical Circuits and Robotics (DISCOVER), pp. 30–35
Dataset: BBC News Summary dataset: 2,225 articles across business, entertainment, politics, sport and technology
Evaluation metrics: ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2 and ROUGE-L precision, recall and F1
Major findings: The paper reports F1 scores of 0.68, 0.60 and 0.67 for ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2 and ROUGE-L respectively on its BBC test setting.
Limitations: Input length was constrained to 512 words; single historical BBC corpus limits domain coverage. IEEE access is institution-dependent; the author-uploaded copy and metadata were reviewed.
Relevance to this project: Motivates reference-summary evaluation, explicit context-window handling and a transparent transformer fallback.
Research gap identified: Long-document chunking, cross-domain validation, factual consistency and laptop latency require direct engineering treatment.

Paper title: Explainable Detection of Fake News on Social Media Using Pyramidal Co-Attention Network
Authors: Fazlullah Khan; Ryan Alturki; Gautam Srivastava; Foziah Gazzawe; Syed Tauhid Ullah Shah; Spyridon Mastorakis
Publisher/conference/journal: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems, vol. 11, no. 4, pp. 4574–4583 (early access 2022)
Dataset: FakeNewsNet: PolitiFact and GossipCop news with user comments; items with at least three comments
Method/model: Pyramidal sentence-comment co-attention with top-k check-worthy sentence/comment explanations
Evaluation metrics: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1; MAP, NDCG and precision for explanation ranking
Major findings: The full text reports a 5.56% relative F1 improvement over a comparison method and gains of 16.4% NDCG and 22.1% precision for top-k comment explanations.
Limitations: Requires social comments that may be unavailable, delayed, noisy or manipulable; explanation rankings are not causal evidence.
Relevance to this project: Directly motivates showing influential text while separating a risk prediction from verified truth.
Research gap identified: A local, article-only explanation is needed when social context is unavailable, with explicit user-facing uncertainty.

Authors: Jing Yang; Didier Vega-Oliveros; Taís Seibt; Anderson Rocha
Dataset: Fool-Me-Twice (FM2), 12,968 claims with associated gold evidence
Method/model: BART-large question-answer generation, extractive QA, MPNet answer comparison and question attention
Evaluation metrics: Development/test macro accuracy over five runs; qualitative attention inspection
Major findings: The explainable attention model reached 73.43±0.83 test accuracy, close to the 74.58±1.66 black-box baseline, while exposing question/answer comparisons.
Limitations: Uses gold rather than retrieved evidence; repetitive or incorrect generated questions remain possible.
Relevance to this project: Defines the stronger evidence-based direction beyond linguistic classification and supports explicit explanation boundaries.
Research gap identified: End-to-end evidence retrieval, calibration and human evaluation must be integrated before claims can be fact-checked reliably.

Paper title: Advancing Fake News Detection: Hybrid Deep Learning With FastText and Explainable AI
Authors: Ehtesham Hashmi; Sule Yildirim Yayilgan; Muhammad Mudassar Yamin; Subhan Ali; Mohamed Abomhara
Method/model: Supervised/unsupervised FastText with ML/DL models; CNN-LSTM champion; LDA and LIME explanations
Evaluation metrics: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1, confusion matrix; topic coherence and perplexity
Major findings: The paper reports CNN-LSTM accuracy around 0.99 on WELFake and FakeNewsNet, outperforming cited 0.97 baselines, and uses LIME to inspect decisions.
Limitations: Very high within-dataset results may still reflect topical/outlet artefacts; deep hybrids are heavier than a student-laptop linear baseline.
Relevance to this project: Supports model comparison, hyperparameter tuning, local explanations and cautious interpretation of high benchmark scores.
Research gap identified: Publisher/event-separated external validation and explanation-fidelity studies are required for real-world trust.

Paper title: Understanding the Use and Abuse of Social Media: Generalized Fake News Detection With a Multichannel Deep Neural Network
Authors: Rohit Kumar Kaliyar; Anurag Goswami; Pratik Narang; Vinay Chamola
Publisher/conference/journal: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems, vol. 11, no. 4, pp. 4878–4887 (early access 2022)
Method/model: Multichannel 1D-CNN with multiple n-gram resolutions and dense layers
Evaluation metrics: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1, false-positive rate and false-negative rate
Major findings: Reported MCNN accuracy was 90.10% on PHEME, 98.20% on FN-COV and 90.10% on CoAID; dataset-specific variation remained substantial.
Limitations: Text-only, binary, model-oriented evaluation; testing several datasets is not the same as training on one publisher group and testing on an unseen group. Institute access should be verified.
Relevance to this project: Reinforces multi-dataset generalisation analysis and reporting more than accuracy alone.
Research gap identified: Stronger cross-event/cross-publisher protocols, multimodal context and calibrated abstention are still needed.

Paper title: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training for Natural Language Generation, Translation, and Comprehension
Authors: Mike Lewis; Yinhan Liu; Naman Goyal; Marjan Ghazvininejad; Abdelrahman Mohamed; Omer Levy; Veselin Stoyanov; Luke Zettlemoyer
Publisher/conference/journal: Association for Computational Linguistics, ACL 2020, pp. 7871–7880
Dataset: Multiple generation/comprehension benchmarks, including CNN/DailyMail and XSum summarization
Method/model: Denoising encoder-decoder Transformer with bidirectional encoder and autoregressive decoder
Evaluation metrics: ROUGE for summarization plus task-specific generation and comprehension metrics
Major findings: BART's text-infilling and sentence-permutation pretraining produced strong results across generation tasks and established the architecture behind DistilBART.
Limitations: Large pretrained models add download size, memory, latency and potential hallucination; benchmark overlap does not ensure factuality.
Relevance to this project: Provides the technical foundation for the optional DistilBART branch and justifies an extractive fallback.
Research gap identified: Long-input, factuality-aware, CPU-efficient inference needs additional engineering beyond the base architecture.

Paper title: Automatic Fake News Detection: Are Models Learning to Reason?
Authors: Casper Hansen; Christian Hansen; Lucas Chaves Lima
Dataset: Political fact-checking datasets with claims and evidence
Method/model: Controlled claim-only, evidence-only and claim-plus-evidence experiments with neural fact-checking models
Major findings: Evidence-only input often performed best; including the claim was negligible or harmful, revealing dataset/evidence shortcuts rather than assured reasoning.
Limitations: Focuses on specific political fact-checking benchmarks and does not itself solve robust evidence retrieval.
Relevance to this project: Directly supports source-shortcut mitigation, independent module boundaries and a prominent generalisation warning.
Research gap identified: Benchmarks and splits must test reasoning and unseen domains rather than reward stable annotation artefacts.

Paper title: Don’t Give Me the Details, Just the Summary! Topic-Aware Convolutional Neural Networks for Extreme Summarization
Authors: Shashi Narayan; Shay B. Cohen; Mirella Lapata
Dataset: XSum: 226,711 BBC articles from 2010–2017 with one-sentence summaries
Method/model: Topic-aware convolutional encoder-decoder for extreme abstractive summarization
Major findings: Introduced a news benchmark deliberately unfavorable to extractive strategies and reported gains over extractive and abstractive baselines.
Limitations: Single broadcaster and historical period; one-sentence references can penalize useful extractive summaries and encourage aggressive abstraction.
Relevance to this project: Provides the legitimate reference-summary dataset used for the measured 150-row evaluation.
Research gap identified: ROUGE should be paired with factual-consistency, coherence, latency and domain-diversity evaluation.

Paper title: ‘Liar, Liar Pants on Fire’: A New Benchmark Dataset for Fake News Detection
Dataset: LIAR: 12.8K decade-spanning, manually labelled PolitiFact short statements with metadata
Method/model: Text baselines and a hybrid CNN combining statement text with metadata
Evaluation metrics: Multi-class classification accuracy and related benchmark comparisons
Major findings: Introduced a public six-label benchmark and showed that combining metadata with text can improve a text-only deep model.
Limitations: Short political claims are not full news articles; metadata can become a shortcut and six labels require mapping for binary use.
Relevance to this project: Explains why LIAR was evaluated but ISOT was selected for full-article binary classification.
Research gap identified: Full-article, source-diverse, event-grouped labels with transparent annotation and licensing remain scarce.
